timeHealth.title: Attendance Time Health
timeHealth.subtitle: DRAIS checks every batch against this school's learned arrival pattern — drift is caught before wrong times are trusted.
timeHealth.wrongTimestamps: ⚠ The system believes today's timestamps are wrong ({{conf}}% drift confidence). No corrections have been applied.

timeHealth.showEvidence: Show device vs DRAIS time (first/last punches)

timeHealth.selectiveIntro: Tick the people whose time is wrong, set the correction, then apply — everyone else stays untouched.
timeHealth.noPunchesForDay: No punches found for this device on this day.
timeHealth.previousLateWarn: The people below currently show as arriving late last night — that's very likely today's early arrival, mis-clocked. Tick them and shift forward to move them onto today.
timeHealth.baselineNote: Baselines are learned from up to 90 days of this school's own history and sharpen after every confirmed correction. Original device timestamps are always preserved.
timeHealth.whatTime: What time did the first arrivals actually begin today?
timeHealth.punchesCorrected: {{n}} punches will be corrected. Undo is available afterwards.
timeHealth.analyzeHint: Scans already-stored punches for days whose clock reading jumped mid-day (a failing-RTC signature) rather than drifted smoothly. Nothing is changed until you preview and confirm a day.
timeHealth.analyzeClean: No jump patterns found in this window.
timeHealth.analyzeAmbiguous: No clear majority reading — needs a manual look, not a guess.
timeHealth.evidenceLine: {{days}} days of history analyzed · last sync {{sync}}
timeHealth.rolloverSuspected: Today's earliest records look like previous-day stragglers, not genuine arrivals.
timeHealth.simulationEvidence: As currently dated: {{cur}}% confidence. Interpreted as belonging to the prior day: {{shifted}}% confidence.
timeHealth.simulationNote: This is a simulation only — nothing has been changed. Review the affected device(s) below and correct manually if you agree.

settings.presenceHelp: Boarding students generally reside at school. {{daily}} (default) means a boarding student still needs a biometric punch like anyone else. {{continuous}} means a boarding student who is checked in stays policy-recognized present on days with no new punch, until checked out or put on leave — check a student in or record leave from their profile. settings.savedWithRule: The choices above (population and manual check-in presence) are part of the attendance rule and are saved with it.

CORRECT_BY_DRIFT.label: Correct by drift
CORRECT_BY_DRIFT.hint: Trust device time unless it reads in the future; recover the real time from learned drift. Best default.

TRUST_DEVICE_TIME.label: Trust device time
TRUST_DEVICE_TIME.hint: Store exactly what the device reports. Never correct. Use only if every device clock is reliable.

TRUST_SERVER_RECEIVE_TIME.label: Trust server time
TRUST_SERVER_RECEIVE_TIME.hint: Stamp every punch with the moment DRAIS received it. Accurate for realtime, wrong for offline backlog.

MANUAL_REVIEW_IF_DRIFT.label: Flag for review
MANUAL_REVIEW_IF_DRIFT.hint: Keep device time but flag punches that drift beyond the limit for a human to check.

ADAPTIVE_DRIFT_NO_MEMORY.label: Adaptive (unstable clock)
ADAPTIVE_DRIFT_NO_MEMORY.hint: For a device with a failing RTC battery whose clock jumps between unrelated readings instead of drifting smoothly. Never trusts a remembered offset from an earlier batch — only ever corrects using fresh evidence from the current batch of punches; if there isn’t enough yet, keeps the safe fallback instead of guessing from stale memory.

timePolicy.title: Device Time Policy
timePolicy.intro: Controls how DRAIS interprets biometric device clocks. Raw device time, server-received time, and the corrected time are always stored — this only chooses which one attendance uses, and whether DRAIS may change the device clock.
timePolicy.whenWrong: When the device clock is wrong
timePolicy.maxDriftHelp: Beyond this, a clock is treated as faulty (correct/flag depending on policy).
timePolicy.autoSyncHint: When ON, DRAIS pushes the correct time to a drifting device. OFF = DRAIS never changes your machine's clock.
timePolicy.backlogHint: Keep original timestamps for punches uploaded after the device was offline.
timePolicy.showBothHint: Display both the device's reported time and the corrected time in logs.

REBOOT.notes: Device restarts immediately. No acknowledgment returned — confirmed by heartbeat gap.

INFO.desc: Request device specs (firmware, user/FP/record counts, IP)
INFO.notes: Device responds with INFO= in next GET heartbeat, not via devicecmd. Format: Ver,UserCount,FPCount,AttCount,IP,...

CHECK.notes: Returns -1007 (data not exist). Not implemented on K40 Pro firmware.

SyncTime.name: Sync Time
SyncTime.notes: Device syncs clock to server time.

SyncUserIdentity.name: Sync User Identity
SyncUserIdentity.desc: Push or update a user on the device
SyncUserIdentity.notes: Tab-separated parameters. PIN is the device user ID. Returns 0 on success.

QueryUsers.name: Query Users
QueryUsers.desc: Request list of all enrolled users from device
QueryUsers.notes: Device responds with table=USERINFO POST containing all user records.

ClearLogs.name: Clear Logs
ClearLogs.desc: Delete attendance logs from device memory
ClearLogs.notes: Clears attendance records. Use with caution.

ClearAllData.name: Clear All Data
ClearAllData.desc: Delete ALL data from device (users, FPs, logs)
ClearAllData.notes: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE — Removes all users, fingerprints, and logs.

ENROLL.notes: Returns -1002 (unsupported command). Not available on K40 Pro.

ENROLLFP.notes: Returns 6 (DATA_NOT_EXIST). Command recognized but not functional.

ENROLLBIO.notes: Returns -1003 (parameter error). Command IS recognized (not -1002) but no parameter format accepted. Tested 17 variants including: space/tab/ampersand separators, with/without FID/TYPE/RETRY/OVERWRITE/NAME/MESSION, zero-padded PIN, positional args, bare command. Push version 2.4.1 likely lacks full ENROLL_BIO implementation — requires firmware upgrade to push v3.x+.

FPviaOPERLOG.name: FP via OPERLOG
FPviaOPERLOG.desc: Device pushes fingerprint templates after local enrollment
FPviaOPERLOG.notes: After enrolling a finger locally on the device, it pushes FP PIN={id}\tFID={n}\tSize={s}\tValid=1\tTMP={base64} via OPERLOG. DRAIS captures and stores these automatically.

templatev10POST.notes: Handler ready in DRAIS to capture templates from table=templatev10 POST. Not yet triggered — depends on successful ENROLL_BIO.

biodataPOST.notes: Handler ready in DRAIS to capture templates from table=biodata POST. Not yet triggered — depends on successful remote enrollment.

st.fallbackHelp: Used only as a last resort (see the banner above) — not while Control Center has this school routed to a central provider.
st.apiKeyHelp: Stored per school. Without it, SMS falls back to server env vars (and fails if none are set). Leave blank to keep the saved key.
st.testHelp: Sends a real test SMS through the provider shown above{{provider}}, using this school's sender ID.
st.autoModeHelp: When on, events with auto_send rules fire immediately. When off, every message is staged for manual approval.
st.quietHelp: During quiet hours, auto messages are queued instead of sent.
st.alertsIntro: You can already see whether each message was delivered, for free, in {{outbox}} and in the pop-up notices on this screen. This option is only for when you also want a {{text}} telling you what happened to a message.
st.costWarning: This costs extra SMS — please read before turning it on
st.secondSms: a second SMS that your school pays for
st.li1: Every alert is {{second}}{{price}}, on top of the message sent to the parent.
st.li2: {{choice}} is the cheap choice: you pay only when something goes wrong.
st.li3: {{choice}} can double your SMS bill: one SMS to the parent, plus one alert to you for each message.
st.li4: To protect you, DRAIS sends {{cap}}{{perHour}}. On a busy morning the rest are skipped, but they still show in SMS Outbox.
